beats.say: England need a massive 68-point swing but coach Brian McDermott says don't chase the points.
After a 30-12 loss to Tonga they roared back with an 82-0 demolition of France.
That leaves them 68 points behind Samoa on points difference with only Papua New Guinea remaining.

beats.say: McDermott told reporters that obsessing over the margin would disrupt their shape and discipline.
Sky Sports adds that PNG are well coached by Jason Demetriou and will not roll over.
The surprising truth: England's only path is to forget the calculator and play their own game.
Could you ignore the scoreboard when a 68-point swing is the only thing that matters?

facts: England face Papua New Guinea in Wollongong on Friday needing a big win to keep semi-final hopes alive.
Brian McDermott has warned his England side not to chase the points as they look to keep their slim Rugby League World Cup hopes alive.
England defeated France 82-0 in their second game of the tournament.
England lost 30-12 to Tonga in their opening game.
England need to make up a 68-point deficit on Samoa.
Papua New Guinea are well coached by Jason Demetriou.
